name: South Face
approach: From the Beverly Turnpike Trailhead (Bean Creek/Beverly Creek TH) off the North Fork Teanaway River Road (FR-9737-112), the approach is well-documented with concrete checkpoints: at about 0.5 mile, bear left onto signed Trail #1391 (Beverly Turnpike Trail) — a wrong fork onto the Bean Creek Trail here is a commonly reported mistake, so double-check the sign. At about 3.1 miles, turn right onto Trail #1226.1 (Fourth Creek Trail). At about 3.6 miles you crest Fourth Creek Pass with the first open views of Argonaut, Colchuck, and Dragontail. Continue down the far side to about 6 miles and ~4,200 ft, where you ford Ingalls Creek (wading or a footlog) to reach good flat camping at the Fourth Creek/Ingalls Creek confluence — day one is roughly 6 miles and 2,000 ft of gain. From camp, follow the Ingalls Creek Trail west for about half a mile, then cut sharply left (north) and start climbing straight upslope toward Argonaut's south face: expect brushy 'jackstraw' forest for the first 300 vertical feet and then dense slide alder for close to 1,000 feet above that (progress can slow to a few hundred feet per hour in the thick of it — stay right/climber's-right to minimize brush where possible). At about 5,200 ft the brush relents onto open slopes; ascend the left side of a large drainage gully up to about 6,600 ft, then continue up the gully itself. At about 7,100 ft the gully forks — the standard line is the left branch (the right also goes but is less traveled). At the base of the summit face, start in the rightmost and larger of two short left-facing corners and climb about three pitches of blocky rock to the summit. The 50-foot chockstone gully that tops out on the east ridge (Class 4, stepping right at the overhang) is the finish of the scramble route, not part of this climb; it is the usual way down. Hazards: the Ingalls Creek ford, sustained brush-bashing on the lower slopes, and possible snow in the gully in shoulder season (carry an axe/crampons if conditions warrant).

approach_variants.name: Beverly Turnpike and Fourth Creek Pass to an Ingalls Creek camp, then straight up the south side
approach_variants.notes:
From the Beverly Turnpike trailhead at the end of FR-9737-112 off the North Fork Teanaway Road, at about 0.5 mile bear left onto signed Trail #1391. Taking the Bean Creek fork here is a commonly reported mistake, so read the sign.

At about 3.1 miles turn right onto Trail #1226.1, the Fourth Creek Trail; at about 3.6 miles you crest Fourth Creek Pass with the first open views of Argonaut, Colchuck and Dragontail. Descend the far side to roughly 6 miles and 4,200 ft, ford Ingalls Creek, and camp at the Fourth Creek confluence. Day one is about 6 miles and 2,000 ft.

From camp, follow the Ingalls Creek Trail west about half a mile, then cut sharply left and north and climb straight upslope. Expect roughly 300 vertical feet of tangled forest and then close to 1,000 ft of dense slide alder above that — progress can drop to a few hundred feet an hour.

At about 5,200 ft the brush relents. Climb the left side of a large drainage gully to about 6,600 ft, then the gully itself.
approach_variants.season: Roughly Jul-Sep. The brush is the reason: it is impassably wet in early season and the gully may hold snow in the shoulders
hazards: Close to 1,000 ft of dense slide alder above 300 ft of jackstraw forest — the defining feature of the day
An Ingalls Creek ford that can be cold and swift early, and ice-covered in the shoulders
Loose blocks low on the route
Possible snow in the gully in the shoulder seasons — carry axe and crampons if in doubt
The descent rappels a chockstone gully where ropes are reported to hang up on the chockstone
A heavily worn sling anchor above that chockstone: inspect and back it up
approach_variants.baseFinding:
Two tests, one at the gully fork and one at the wall, and you need both.

First, the fork at about 7,100 ft. The gully you have been climbing splits. The standard line is the left branch. The right branch also reaches the mountain but is far less travelled, so a party that drifts right will find progressively less sign of passage — that absence is the signal to come back down and cross over.

Second, the wall itself, and this is the one that matters in fog because the gully fork can be ambiguous under snow. At the base of the south face there are two short left-facing corners side by side. The route starts in the rightmost and larger of the two. Not a corner — two corners, and you take the bigger, right-hand one. If there is only one corner in front of you, you are not at the start.

What the climbing should feel like, as a check on all of the above: blocky, generally solid rock, three pitches, graded 5.6 — but an old-school 5.6 that parties consistently report climbing like modern 5.9 or harder. So sustained-feeling climbing is not evidence you are off route here. Watch for a few loose blocks low down.

A separate feature worth not confusing with the start: high on the mountain there is a 50-foot gully with a chockstone near its top, Class 4, taken by stepping right at the overhang, which tops out on the east ridge a short way from the summit. That is the finish of the ordinary scramble line, and the approach description on this route describes it as though it were the route. It is not the base of the 5.6 face climb, and a party navigating to it will end up on the scramble.

waypoints.name: Beverly Turnpike Trailhead
waypoints.note: Shared trailhead with Bean Creek Basin at the end of the rough, overgrown FR 9737-112 spur road.
waypoints.directions: From the North Fork Teanaway River Road, turn onto the FR-9737-112 spur and follow it to its end at the Beverly Turnpike trailhead, around 3,650 ft. The spur is rough and overgrown, and the gravel access opens with spring snowmelt; that plus the Ingalls Creek ford further along makes July through September the practical window. It is the shared lot with Bean Creek Basin, so at about half a mile bear left onto signed Trail #1391 rather than taking the Bean Creek fork, which is a commonly reported mistake here.

waypoints.name: Beverly Creek Trail (FST 1391) / Fourth Creek Trail (FST 1226.1) junction
waypoints.note: Faint fork in forested/open terrain; bear toward Fourth Creek Trail for the pass rather than continuing up Beverly Creek.

waypoints.name: Fourth Creek Pass
waypoints.note: Low, treed pass on the drainage divide reached via a steep final 0.3-mile push; descends into the Fourth Creek drainage on the far side.

waypoints.name: Fourth Creek / Ingalls Creek confluence camp
waypoints.note: Established basecamp near the creek confluence used by most south-side parties before the summit push.

waypoints.name: Ingalls Creek ford
waypoints.note: Potentially dangerous ford — cold and swift in early season, can be partially frozen with slick ice-covered rocks.

waypoints.name: South-side gully, west of the main gully
waypoints.note: Class 2 scrambling up loose rock in the gully just west of Argonaut's main south gully, heading for the summit ridge.

waypoints.name: Argonaut Peak summit (west summit, true)
waypoints.note: Final moves onto the true (west) summit ridge are harder than the class 2 approach suggests, often low class 3/4.
